reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    State: Oregon
    Focus year: 2021

    Question: For tenants residing in properties that go into foreclosure,
    does the law require longer-than-usual notice?
*/

% -----------------------------
% Basic helpers (no modules)
% -----------------------------

greater_than(A, B) :- number(A), number(B), A > B.

% -----------------------------
% Scenario facts (question statement)
% -----------------------------

state(oregon).
focus_year(2021).

% A residential property goes into foreclosure (trust deed foreclosure sale context).
property(p1).
foreclosure_sale_scheduled(p1).

% The property includes dwelling units subject to ORS chapter 90 (residential landlord-tenant).
subject_to_ors_chapter_90(p1).

% Tenant resides/occupies the property.
tenant(t1).
occupies_as_residential_tenant(t1, p1).

% To apply the tenant-protection language in ORS 86.771(10)'s mandated tenant notice,
% the tenant must be a "bona fide tenant" (as described in the statutory notice text).
% We encode it as facts satisfying those conditions.
borrower(owner1).
not_borrower(t1).                % tenant is not the borrower/property owner
not_close_family_of_borrower(t1). % not child/spouse/parent of borrower
arms_length_rental_agreement(t1).
rent_not_substantially_below_fmr_or_subsidized(t1).
rental_agreement_entered_before_foreclosure_sale(t1).

% Lease type (needed to determine 30 vs 60 days in the statute's tenant-protection notice).
% The question is general; we instantiate a common covered case: a bona fide tenant with a fixed term lease.
tenancy_type(t1, fixed_term).

% Whether the post-foreclosure new owner wants to move in as primary residence (affects notice length).
% In this scenario, assume no (so fixed-term tenant gets 60 days under the statute text).
new_owner_primary_residence_intent(p1, no).

/* scenario_statement/0
   Succeeds when the question scenario (as encoded) holds. */
scenario_statement :-
    state(oregon),
    focus_year(2021),
    property(p1),
    foreclosure_sale_scheduled(p1),
    subject_to_ors_chapter_90(p1),
    tenant(t1),
    occupies_as_residential_tenant(t1, p1).

% -----------------------------
% Statute translation (Oregon, 2021)
% -----------------------------

/* OR Rev Stat  86.771(10) (2021)
   If the property includes one or more dwelling units subject to ORS chapter 90,
   the notice of sale must include a notice addressed to occupants who are or might be residential tenants,
   including information concerning the right to notice under ORS 86.782(6)(c).

   We encode the operative condition that triggers tenant-protective notice content:
   property subject to ORS ch 90 => required to provide tenant-facing notice in sale notice.
*/
statute_or_86_771_2021_requires_tenant_notice_in_sale_notice(Property) :-
    subject_to_ors_chapter_90(Property).

/* The statute-mandated tenant notice text (embedded in  86.771(10)) states, in substance:
   - After the foreclosure sale, the new owner must provide written termination notice.
   - If bona fide tenant:
       * fixed term lease => right to continue for 60 days from date given written termination notice; OR
       * month-to-month or week-to-week => at least 30 days from date given written termination notice.
   - If new owner wants to move in as primary residence => may require move-out after 30 days even with fixed term.
   We encode these durations as deterministic rules for required minimum days after termination notice.
*/

% bona_fide_tenant/1 encoded from the statutory notice text definition
bona_fide_tenant(Tenant) :-
    tenant(Tenant),
    not_borrower(Tenant),
    not_close_family_of_borrower(Tenant),
    arms_length_rental_agreement(Tenant),
    rent_not_substantially_below_fmr_or_subsidized(Tenant),
    rental_agreement_entered_before_foreclosure_sale(Tenant).

/* required_notice_days_after_foreclosure_sale/3
   required_notice_days_after_foreclosure_sale(Tenant, Property, Days)
   captures the minimum time the tenant may remain AFTER receiving the new owner's written termination notice,
   per the tenant-protection text required by ORS 86.771(10) (referencing ORS 86.782(6)(c)). */
required_notice_days_after_foreclosure_sale(Tenant, Property, 30) :-
    bona_fide_tenant(Tenant),
    occupies_as_residential_tenant(Tenant, Property),
    new_owner_primary_residence_intent(Property, yes),
    !.
required_notice_days_after_foreclosure_sale(Tenant, Property, 60) :-
    bona_fide_tenant(Tenant),
    occupies_as_residential_tenant(Tenant, Property),
    new_owner_primary_residence_intent(Property, no),
    tenancy_type(Tenant, fixed_term),
    !.
required_notice_days_after_foreclosure_sale(Tenant, Property, 30) :-
    bona_fide_tenant(Tenant),
    occupies_as_residential_tenant(Tenant, Property),
    tenancy_type(Tenant, month_to_month),
    !.
required_notice_days_after_foreclosure_sale(Tenant, Property, 30) :-
    bona_fide_tenant(Tenant),
    occupies_as_residential_tenant(Tenant, Property),
    tenancy_type(Tenant, week_to_week),
    !.

% -----------------------------
% "Usual" notice baseline (for comparison)
% -----------------------------

/* For purposes of the question ("longer-than-usual notice"), we use a baseline
   "usual" minimum termination notice of 30 days for ordinary periodic tenancies.
   This baseline is used only for the comparative question, not to restate ORS ch 90 fully. */
usual_minimum_notice_days_oregon(30).

% -----------------------------
% Reasoning: does foreclosure require longer-than-usual notice?
% -----------------------------

foreclosure_tenant_notice_days(Property, Tenant, Days) :-
    foreclosure_sale_scheduled(Property),
    occupies_as_residential_tenant(Tenant, Property),
    statute_or_86_771_2021_requires_tenant_notice_in_sale_notice(Property),
    required_notice_days_after_foreclosure_sale(Tenant, Property, Days).

requires_longer_than_usual_notice(Property, Tenant) :-
    foreclosure_tenant_notice_days(Property, Tenant, Days),
    usual_minimum_notice_days_oregon(Usual),
    greater_than(Days, Usual).

% -----------------------------
% Output predicate
% -----------------------------

housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    requires_longer_than_usual_notice(p1, t1),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    scenario_statement,
    !.

% -----------------------------
% Main entrypoint (required)
% -----------------------------

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: For tenants residing in properties that go into foreclosure, does the law require longer-than-usual notice?
